name: Paltiel
overview: Paltiel was a male leader from the tribe of Issachar, recognized for his role in the apportioning of the Promised Land. He is specifically noted in Numbers 34:26 as representing his tribe in this important task. His leadership highlights the organized division of the land among the tribes of Israel under God's guidance.
namesAndTitles: The name Paltiel means 'G-d [El] is [my] deliverance,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that emphasizes God's saving power. This proper name underscores a personal trust in divine deliverance, consistent with the faith of Israel's leaders.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Paltiel as the father of Azzan, as recorded in Numbers 34:26. Beyond this explicit relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Paltiel's significance lies in his leadership role during the critical period when the Israelites were preparing to enter and settle the Promised Land. As the appointed leader of Issachar, he was entrusted with the responsibility of ensuring his tribe received its allotted inheritance. This task was essential to fulfilling God's promise to Israel and maintaining order among the tribes. His role exemplifies faithful stewardship and obedience to God's commands in the unfolding narrative of Israel's history.
